newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dassault says Aerospatiale merger still on agenda.
newsitem.headline: Dassault says Aerospatiale merger still on agenda.

text.p: French combat plane maker Dassault Aviation said on Tuesday that a planned merger with state-owned Aerospatiale was still on the agenda.

"Serge Dassault declares that contrary to comments attributed to him, the merger between Aerospatiale and Dassault is still on the agenda and will be the subject of discussions to come between the government and himself," a Dassault spokesman told Reuters.
Dassault met French transport minister Jean-Claude Gayssot on Monday, the spokesman said, but gave no further details. Further meetings were planned but had not yet been arranged, he added.
The merger plan was due to have been announced at the Paris Air Show, starting June 14, Aerospatiale executives have said.

But with the arrival of a Socialist government hostile to privatisations, grave doubts overhang the merger plan. Gayssot, a Communist, has said he prefers public service solutions over privatisations.

Dassault had made a privatisation of the merged Aerospatiale Dassault group a condition for agreeing to the merger, otherwise it would mean an effective nationalisation of family-controlled Dassault Aviation .

Under the merger plan presented to the previous conservative government, Dassault was expected to hold around 20 percent of the capital of the enlarged aerospace group, which would have annual sales of 70 billion francs.
The Aerospatiale Dassault merger was announced by President Jacques Chirac in April 1996, as part of a consolidation of France's fragmented defence industry.
